display.title: Episode 486: Rabbi Akiva's Negel Vasser and the Drunken Father (The Three Weeks)
display.summary_short: A Three Weeks program without music: Rabbi Akiva washes his hands in prison, his great rule of loving one's fellow Jew, and a story with no happy ending about learning not to copy bad ways.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during the Three Weeks, so the program opens without its usual music and has no march. Uncle Yossi invites children to join Tzivos Hashem, whose soldiers fight the yetzer hara with Torah and mitzvos. A brother and sister say the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. The first story tells how Rabbi Akiva, jailed for teaching Torah and given no water for three days, used his precious jug of water to wash his hands and make a brachah; the amazed ruler freed him and made him an advisor. Uncle Yossi then explains Rabbi Akiva's great rule, 'Love your fellow as yourself', and the Alter Rebbe's teaching that Ahavas Yisroel leads to love of Hashem. A second story, 'with no happy ending', tells of Naftali, who leads his father, a drinker, to see a drunk lying in the street, only to hear him ask where to get such a good drink. Like the Torah's warning not to follow the ways of Egypt and Canaan, we are shown bad ways only so we will not copy them. The show closes by explaining the Three Weeks: the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed through baseless hatred and will be rebuilt through Ahavas Yisroel.
display.lesson: Love every Jew as yourself; this leads to loving Hashem and will bring the rebuilding of the Beis HaMikdash.

date.note: 'The Three Weeks have already begun' and no opening music; one week after episode 485 (13 Tammuz 5751). A Tuesday.

advisories.note: Rabbi Akiva is jailed for teaching Torah and given no food or water for three days.
A boy is ashamed and in tears over his father's drinking.
The Naftali story deliberately ends without the father changing.
Explains the Three Weeks and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash.

privacy.note: Two Shema guests named with their family name.

sources_cited.note: 'Love your fellow as yourself', which Rabbi Akiva calls a great rule of the Torah.
Rabbi Akiva's saying 'zeh klal gadol baTorah', cited as found in the Gemara.
Do not follow the practices of Egypt and Canaan; cited as Parshas Acharei, chapter 18.
The Alter Rebbe: Ahavas Yisroel leads to Ahavas Hashem.
The Beis HaMikdash was destroyed because of baseless hatred, cited as what the Chachamim tell us.

segments.title: Love Your Fellow as Yourself

segments.title: The Drunken Father
segments.summary: Naftali shows his father a drunk in the street, but the father only asks where to get such a good drink.

segments.title: Not Following the Ways of Egypt and Canaan
segments.summary: The Torah shows us bad ways only so we will reject them and be an example to the world.

segments.title: The Three Weeks: Rebuilding with Ahavas Yisroel
